description: Echoes of Orbit tells the stories of NASA’s abandoned rovers & probes on the Moon and Mars for school-age space fans. 🚀 Website, design & videos are covered. We need: ✍️ a writer, 🔍 a fact-checker, 🛰️ a space nerd, 🎓 a kid-friendly explainer. Early members get real say in the story. Beginners welcome! Join request: tell us your favorite abandoned spacecraft.
summary:
Echoes of the Orbit answers “Abandoned but not Forgotten” by turning NASA’s silent machines into stories school-age students can explore. Playing as a Cadet in the fictional Starun Echo Division, users watch a cinematic intro before entering Mission Control to recover stories of spacecraft humanity left behind.

Machine Stories covers 22 NASA machines across Mars (Opportunity, Spirit, Pathfinder & Sojourner, Viking landers, Phoenix, InSight, Ingenuity, Mars Polar Lander), the Moon (Apollo sites, Lunar Roving Vehicles, Surveyor landers, impact sites), and deep space (Pioneer 10 & 11, Voyager 1 & 2). Each card shows its status (went silent, finished its mission, left behind, lost on arrival, still traveling) across three reading levels: Explorer (classes 1–5), Pilot (6–9), and Commander (10–12). Cards cover how each worked, what we learned, a line in the machine’s own voice, and a direct NASA source link. Built-in accessibility includes keyboard navigation, readable text, subtitles, mute controls, and reduced-motion support.

How we built it: React, Vite, Tailwind, Framer Motion, and Zustand, using a data-driven archive sourced from NASA Science, NASA JPL (including the MER 3D model), and the NASA History Program Moon catalogue.

AI Disclosure: We used Google Gemini (images), Google Flow with Veo 3 (video experiments), Google Antigravity (coding), and Claude (planning and fact-checking against NASA sources). No real people’s faces or voices were used.
details:
Echoes of the Orbit is an interactive, 3D space-story web experience that turns NASA’s public domain archives into a playable Cadet mission. Built with React, Three.js, and verified NASA/JPL-Caltech data, it lets learners explore the engineering, scientific breakthroughs, and human stories behind 22 historic spacecraft left across our solar system.

Stepping into the Starun Echo Division Mission Control, users navigate 3D planetary destinations—Mars (The Silent Dunes), the Moon (The Tranquil Basins), and Deep Space (The Drifting Probes)—to recover lost signals from pioneers like Opportunity, Spirit, Viking, Pathfinder, and Voyager. Each spacecraft dossier features telemetry timelines, engineering breakdowns (How It Worked), discoveries (What We Learned), and first-person storytelling (In Its Own Voice).

To make NASA science accessible to every student, an adaptive reading toggle scales explanations across Explorer (Grades 3–5), Pilot (Grades 6–8), and Commander (Grades 9–12). A transparent Sources & AI log documents all NASA datasets alongside clear disclosures for how Gemini, Veo 3, Claude, and Antigravity IDE assisted with curriculum pedagogy, transit visuals, and frontend architecture.
